newsitem.title: UK: Metals trend lower, await LME April pricing.
newsitem.headline: Metals trend lower, await LME April pricing.

text.p: Base metal markets carried on declining during Monday LME pre-market trading, maintaining the soggy trend seen Friday.

Traders said the market was in a negative frame of mind after Friday's mini sell-off, due to bearish charts and expectations of further sales later when "third Wednesday" pricing takes place in the rings.
The opening warehouse stock report for the week showed declines for copper, aluminium, lead and zinc inventories, but this had little real impact.
Business was not over-active, however, with copper losing ground from initially unchanged levels in relatively little volume.
Copper whipped down to $2,255 a tonne, a $17 loss from Friday, but managed to hold above the $2,250 chart support level.
In the short term, prices need to hold above this level to mitigate against a heftier decline.
Aluminium settled around $1,560, down $4 from the pre-weekend close, but trade was thin. Again, prices need to hold this chart point, otherwise a test of $1,535 is on the cards, they said.
Nickel fell sharply, with some sell stops triggered, and prices dropped to around $7,115/35 a tonne, down from Friday's $7,250 close.
Analysts said that bearish pressure emanates from recent rises in LME stocks, which are expected to continue in the short term.
Macquarie Equities noted that the inventory increase follows the release of 5,000/8,000 tonnes of Norilsk nickel impounded by Russian tax authorities last year.
Material is being cut in Rotterdam at the rate of 1,000/1,500 tonnes a week for delivery on to the LME, so several weeks of shipments still remain, Macquarie said.
Elsewhere, lead was trading around $628, up just $1, while zinc was indicated at $1,228/30, against Friday's $1,232 close.
Tin shed $15 to $5,615, while alloy was unchanged at $1,450.
